extra.label: Binder RMSD (binder alone vs complex)
extra.note: BindCraft Binder_RMSD: the binder predicted on its own, compared with its shape in the complex. BindCraft rejects designs above 3.5 Å.
rescue: Re-predict the binder alone with a second model; discard if it still differs from the complex shape

extra.label: Atoms within 3 Å of the other subunit
extra.note: The design is placed on the reference assembly. A binder that overlaps another subunit could not bind the assembled protein. Overlap fails a design; contact at the subunit interface is a warning.
rescue: Add the other subunit as fixed context, or move the binder to a face that stays exposed in the assembly

nl.text: At most 9 atoms within 3 Å of the other subunit

extra.label: Contacted residues at the subunit interface
extra.note: Contacted residues that another subunit buries in the assembly. A surface that is part of the subunit interface may not exist on the assembled protein.
rescue: Keep as a hedge, or discard if the goal is a binder of the intact assembly

extra.label: Atoms within 3 Å of the rest of the protein
extra.note: BindCraft only saw the construct. The rest of the same chain (the removed regions) is placed from the reference structure; a binder that overlaps it could not bind the full-length protein.
rescue: Include the neighbouring domain in the target, or move the binder away from that face

nl.text: At most 9 atoms within 3 Å of the rest of the protein

extra.label: Contacts next to a cut end
extra.note: Contacted residues within a few residues of a cut end of the construct, or of a deleted loop. A surface next to a cut can be exposed only because the rest of the protein is missing.
rescue: Extend the target by 10 to 15 residues and re-run, or discard

extra.label: Contacted residues buried in the full protein
extra.note: Contacted residues that the removed regions would bury (more than the area set in the profile). These contacts may not exist on the full-length protein.
rescue: Include the covering region in the target and re-run

cards.title: Detected: BindCraft · {n_runs} runs
cards.html: {n_designs} accepted sequences in {n_families} backbone families, plus {n_rejected} rejected models kept for near-miss rescue. Families are read from the design names. BindCraft keeps at most 2 accepted sequences per backbone by default. Each run keeps its own settings, hotspots, target construct and diversity estimate.

cards.title: Target frame
cards.html: BindCraft restarts the residue numbering at 1, so the tool maps the numbering of the construct back to the reference structure by sequence. It adds the other subunits and the rest of the chain of the reference structure, and checks every design against them.

cards.title: Read, recomputed, missing
cards.html:
Read: sequences, per-model and average scores, per-residue pLDDT (B-factor), the run settings and the filter counters.
Recomputed from the structures: interface on both chains, H-bonds, buried unsatisfied polars, buried area, hydrophobic patches, loops, termini, liabilities, fold clusters (TM-align), site clusters, overlap with the other subunits and the rest of the chain.
Not available: PAE, ipSAE, an independent pose check, repeat seeds, and often the number of attempted trajectories. The checks that need them are switched off instead of guessed.

text.badge.title.board: Designs and scores come from BindCraft runs. Structures are relaxed AlphaFold2 models, placed on the reference structure. Every score is a screen, not a verdict.
text.badge.title.inspector: Binder models are BindCraft AF2 complexes placed on the reference chain. Contacts, hydrogen bonds, buried polars and context checks are recomputed from the coordinates. BindCraft does not write PAE, so none is shown.
text.badge.title.map: Designs and scores come from BindCraft runs. Where orthologs or paralogs were given, they are UniProt sequences aligned to the target construct and conservation grades are computed from the orthologs only.
text.badge.title.query: Designs and scores come from BindCraft runs, accepted and rejected. Rules are typed and editable; the natural-language box is keyword-based and only fills the same rules.

highlights.text: 2 of 8 accepted designs fail the rest-of-protein check (1 of 5 in run01 and 1 of 3 in run02): 10 or more binder atoms sit within 3 Å of residues outside the construct that BindCraft never saw. 2 of 8 have at least one atom closer than 2.2 Å.

link.filter: largest overlap: 47 atoms within 3 Å of the rest of the protein

highlights.text: No accepted design reaches the other subunit: the closest binder atom is 3.9 Å from it (median 6 Å), so all 8 pass the dimer-overlap check.

link.filter: closest approach to the other subunit

highlights.text: Hotspots touched by the accepted designs. run01 (T113, I115 and L125): T113 is touched by 4 of 5, I115 by 1 and L125 by 1; 0 touch all 3, 1 touches none. run02 (T113, I115, L121 and L125): T113 is touched by 1 of 3, I115 by 1, L121 by 0 and L125 by 0; 0 touch all 4, 2 touch none.

The runs differ in hotspots T113, I115 and L125 against T113, I115, L121 and L125, construct 110 against 102 residues (run02 lacks 79-82 and 139-142) and binder length 60-100 against 62-66. Diversity and the need for more designs are therefore estimated per run and never pooled.

Families, not sequences: run01 has 4 (coverage 0.62, level early) and run02 has 3 (coverage 0.83, level early), measured on fold and site together. The estimates for run01 and run02 are low-confidence (fewer than 30 families). Attempted trajectories are unknown for run01 and run02, so yield is per passed trajectory.
2 of the 3 rejected designs that have a structure (all in run01) are near-miss rescues: a single filter missed by at most 25% of its threshold (1 on shape complementarity and 1 on binder pLDDT).
Sequence screen at the 4 hotspot residues of the runs: ortholog one and ortholog two keep all 4; I115 varies (T in ortholog three); PARA1 matches 1 of the 4.
